paper.title_en: A bidirectional quantum state transmission protocol over butterfly networks with quantum encryption and network coding
paper.abstract_en: With the continuous evolution of quantum networks, information exchange among multiple participants has become a key research focus. In multi-party bidirectional quantum communication, multiple transmission flows are prone to severe path-conflict bottlenecks that degrade network throughput. To alleviate this problem, we select the classic two-pair butterfly network as our communication topology and propose a protocol that integrates quantum teleportation with remote state preparation to achieve bidirectional quantum state transmission over this network. Leveraging shared quantum entanglement, source nodes can simultaneously send their quantum states to corresponding target nodes, while target nodes can transmit their own quantum states back to the respective source nodes, enabling mutual data exchange. The intermediate node performs encoding operation on the received classical messages, reducing classical communication costs by two bits and enhancing overall communication efficiency. This approach better caters to complex communication demands, facilitating instantaneous information exchange with higher efficiency. Participants only need to execute basic quantum operations to complete the communication task, which simplifies practical physical implementation. Additionally, to prevent eavesdroppers from stealing information in the side quantum channel, quantum encryption technology is introduced to protect information during transmission. Security analysis shows that, under the considered attack model and ideal conditions, the protocol can resist attacks from external eavesdroppers as well as internal hostile participants. Within the ideal setup, this protocol supports faithful transmission of both known and unknown arbitrary single-qubit states across the butterfly network and also capitalizes on the distinctive merits of network coding. As a result, it offers a practical solution to the bottleneck issue arising from conflicting communication paths among network nodes.
